description:
Compare tracked GPU rental prices for one model (e.g. 'H100', 'A100 SXM', 'RTX 4090', 'L40S'), cheapest first. If a result looks wrong, give the user its report_issue_url.

Same data as https://thelanternworks.com/api/v1/gpu-prices.json. Sorted by hourly_usd ascending; each result
has source_url and checked_at. 'Cheapest' means cheapest among tracked providers, not the whole market.
limit 1-25. Unknown model returns not_found listing tracked models.
H100/A100: cheapest_by_form_factor gives one pick per form_factor (tier_class, interruptible, in_stock); same rule as the site. 'NVLink' rows are form 'not stated': NVLink is the bridge, and the vendor doesn't say SXM or PCIe.
Each result has tier_class: on-demand | community | marketplace | interruptible (spot/preemptible) |
reserved | dedicated-monthly. Reserved (reservation/commitment 'starting from') rates are left out unless
include_reserved=true, and even then they are never reported as cheapest. DEFAULT on_demand_only=true: results[0] is the cheapest
on-demand rate. Pass on_demand_only=false to include spot/interruptible, community and marketplace capacity (each
such row is labelled by tier_class and interruptible); the summary then names the cheapest on-demand rate when the
overall cheapest isn't. If a model has no on-demand rate, or every on-demand rate needs more GPUs than requested,
the default falls back to all rates and says so in on_demand_fallback.
gpus (optional, 1-1024; default 1, stated in assumptions): the GPU count you need. A rate ranks only when its
min_gpus (smallest allocation sold) is <= gpus; rates sold only as larger allocations (e.g. 8-GPU nodes) are NOT
ranked and are listed in excluded_min_gpus (vendor, gpu, tier, min_gpus, gpu_count, hourly_usd, rate_id, source_url,
checked_at, reason, min_bill_usd_per_hour, min_bill_basis); min_gpus_unmet counts them (also in brief). Pass gpus=8 to
compare 8-GPU nodes. If every rate needs more GPUs, the error says which gpus value ranks them.
Each result has min_bill_usd_per_hour = min_gpus x hourly_usd (min_bill_basis: hourly_rate, per_second_rate or
monthly_equivalent) and effective_at, when the vendor started charging this price (effective_at_basis vendor_stated,
or first_observed = first daily snapshot showing it after a different price, an upper bound; null when not datable),
separate from last_verified. Neither affects ranking.
include_history=true adds each result's price_history (daily-snapshot change points) and history.recent_changes
(price changes for this model among tracked providers, last 30 days) from /api/v1/gpu-prices/history.json.
Each result has data_age_hours (hours since its price was last verified), degraded (> 48 h) and stale (> 7 days).
A degraded row is shown and flagged but never ranked first while a fresh row exists; if none is fresh,
stale_fallback=true and the summary says so.
By default a rate whose price is older than 168 h is never ranked or named cheapest: it is listed in stale_prices
('stale price (N days old)'); if every rate is stale, results is empty and the summary says no current cheapest.
max_data_age_hours (optional) replaces the 168 h default and drops older rates; excluded_too_old counts them.
region (optional): a country/area code ('US', 'EU') matches every published zone in it; a zone code ('US-NE-1', 'us-east-1') matches exactly, any case. Rates whose unexpired published regions exclude it are dropped; rates with no region
evidence stay, labelled unresolved and ranked after the rest. Each result has eligibility {eligible, applied, unmet,
unknown} from the shared T47 contract; constraints.eligible_rate_ids is the same set estimate_job_cost and price
watches use. Unknown stock is not confirmed availability.
model_identity (T61): sourced nominal_memory and usable_memory (vendor-allocatable) for the queried model, each
with source_url; unknown stays 'unknown'. min_usable_memory_gb (optional) keeps only rows whose SOURCED usable
memory meets it; rows with unknown usable memory are counted in usable_memory_filter.unknown and never matched
on nominal memory or vram_gb.
name: compare_gpu_prices

referral_disclosure.description: One-line referral disclosure, present whenever the result names a provider; each provider-naming item then has tracked_url (tagged /go/ redirect).
